item.title: Stochastic switching in quadrupole-trap-based levitodynamic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.01387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We have theoretically investigated the stochastic switching dynamics of a charged microparticle in a quadrupole trap near the principal parametric resonance at atmospheric pressure. We show that this behavior arises from a balance of thermal noise-activated escape and dissipative return between linear and nonlinear dynamical regimes of the particle motion. The switching follows an effective Gibbs distribution with an effective potential barrier between the regimes and effective system temperature, which are both experimentally accessible. Because the effective barrier depends on particle mass and charge, and since thermal noise reveals rather than obscures the transition, this exponential dependence could provide the foundation to precision noise-aware detection schemes. The system further offers a highly adjustable platform for studying activation dynamics in non-equilibrium parametric systems.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Rybin, Semyon Rudyi, Dmitrii Shcherbinin

item.title: Aging and configurational memories at rough frictional interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2510.14769v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Frictional interfaces retain distinct memories of how they were sheared and how long they have rested, yet rate-and-state descriptions typically compress these histories into a single state variable. Here we combine nanometer-per-second sliding experiments on rough multi-asperity contacts with different protocols to disentangle temporal and configurational memories at frictional onset. We identify a broad friction force peak associated with shear-driven reorganization of the load-bearing contact network. By contrast, holding a previously sheared system at rest in an arrested configuration produces a much narrower friction force peak that grows approximately logarithmically with hold time and relaxes over nanometer-scale slip distances. Configurational disorder without waiting regenerates only the broad peak, whereas waiting without configurational disorder generates only the aging peak. These results show that aging and configurational disorder write and read experimentally separable frictional memories, and that static friction is a protocol-dependent quantity rather than a fixed material property.
item.dc:creator: Kasra Farain, Daniel Bonn
